row.assistant_content:
The name **Flagstaff** originates from an event in **August 1876**, during an expedition organized by the U.S. Army Signal Corps to survey a telegraph line route. 

In late summer that year, the party was exploring the high desert plateau east of the San Francisco Peaks in northern Arizona. On **August 20, 1876**, the team erected a tall pine pole topped with a flag on a prominent hill near natural freshwater springs (now the site of downtown Flagstaff). They officially named the location **“Flagstaff”** to mark the spot for future travelers and military/telegraph operations.

Over the following decades, the site grew into a stagecoach stop and then a railroad hub after the arrival of the transcontinental railway in 1882, eventually becoming the incorporated city we know today.
